newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi dinar soars on amnesty to Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi dinar soars on amnesty to Kurds.

text.p: The Iraqi dinar surged on Tuesday following President Saddam Hussein's decision to pardon Iraqi Kurds and remove Baghdad's blockade on the north.
Money changers in Baghdad said the dinar climed to about 1,000 to the dollar in late afternoon trading from 1,350 in early morning.
Traders said they expected prices of essential commodities to fall in the next days as supplies from northern Iraq will start pouring into the rest of the country.

The economy of northern Iraq is based on agriculture and cross-border trade with neighbouring Iran and Turkey. The region is almost self-sufficient in vegetables, fruits and cereals like rice and wheat.
Kurds in the north still deal with Iraqi bank notes printed in Switzerland prior to the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait. Bills in circulation in the rest of the country are printed on local presses.
Each old dinar in circulation in northern Iraq is worth 50 of its post-Gulf War equivalent in other parts of the country.

Iraq's decision to issue an amnesty and lift the embargo followed the sweeping battlefield victories of its new Kurdish militia ally, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), over its old rival, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
